title: Recognition of assets and liabilities under §246 HGB
summary: Lesson two of a ten-part commercial balance sheet course, worked through in depth. Recognition, presentation and measurement are three ordered steps and the order is load-bearing. The statute commands completeness but never defines what an asset or a liability is; case law supplies the three tests for each, and economic ownership decides whose balance sheet an item lands on.
evidence: §246(1) HGB has four sentences, each doing one job; the completeness command is Vollständigkeitsgebot
three asset tests: future economic benefit, independent usability, independent valuability
purchased goodwill 'counts as' an asset by legal fiction: 10 million paid for 8 million of net assets leaves 2 million
movable assets: above 50% business use is mandatory business property, below 10% is mandatory private, between the two it is elective
a 40,000 EUR car at 60% business use enters the balance sheet in full, not at 60%
warranty provision example: 1,000 units sold, 5% return rate, 200 EUR per repair, 10,000 EUR provision
German tax guidance treats a lease base term of 40-90% of useful life as leaving the asset with the lessor
§246(2) forbids offsetting, which is why a valuation unit under §254 works in measurement only, never in presentation
friction: The source video could not be opened and no transcript existed. The narrative was rebuilt from the companion article plus the statutory text, so the skeleton is right but any example the professor gave only on video is missing. The document says so in its first paragraph rather than presenting itself as complete.

The article calls the second asset test 'independent usability'. The settled commercial-law formulation is Einzelverwertbarkeit, separate realisability. Following the article would have hidden why the test exists at all: the creditor is asking what can be sold off separately if the company fails.

Expected the statute to define 'asset' and 'liability'. It does not. From a mathematics background that reads as a theorem with two undefined symbols; in law the text is the axiom and decades of judgments supply the meaning.
notes: Section eight of this document connects §246(2) to the §254 valuation-unit work directly.
